items.title: Quantum tomography of fermion pairs in e + e − collisions: Longitudinal beam polarization effects
items.summary: We present a quantum tomography study of fermion pair production at future $e^+e^-$ colliders, emphasizing how longitudinal beam polarization controls the two-qubit spin density matrix. We study the processes $e^+ e^- \to t\bar{t},\ e^+e^-\to μ^+μ^-$ and Bhabha scattering $e^+e^-\to e^+e^-$, representing the mass threshold behavior, the $Z$ pole resonance and the $s/t$-channel interplay.

items.title: Effects of auditory sensory stimulation on consciousness and physiological parameters among individuals with disorders of consciousness: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: Objective To systematically evaluate the effects of auditory sensory stimulation (SS) on consciousness levels and physiological parameters in patients with disorders of consciousness (DOC). Furthermore, this study aimed to explore intervention characteristics based on the frequency, intensity, time, and type (FITT) framework that may influence treatment effects and to investigate potential sources of between-study heterogeneity.

items.title: Measurement-informed dynamical decoupling for fidelity preservation on large-scale quantum processors
items.summary: Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a key technique for suppressing decoherence and preserving the performance of quantum algorithms. We introduce a measurement-based DD (MDD) protocol that determines control unitary gates from partial measurements of noisy subsystems, with measurement overhead scaling linearly with the number of subsystems.

items.summary: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions.

items.title: Physical predictions in closed quantum gravity
items.summary: A bstract Recent developments in gravitational path integrals indicate that the nonperturbative physical Hilbert space of a closed universe is one-dimensional within each superselection sector. This raises a basic puzzle: how can a unique quantum-gravity state give rise to semiclassical physics, measurement outcomes, and classical probabilities?

items.title: Quantum algorithms
items.summary: This chapter highlights quantum algorithms as a gate-based computational framework that exploits superposition, entanglement, and phase-coherent interference to realize demonstrable complexity reductions on selected problems. It begins by formally distinguishing quantum algorithms from classical deterministic and randomized computation through reversible unitary evolution, oracle-based problem access, and the measurement constraint that collapses quantum state information, thereby motivating amplitude-engineering…

items.title: Quantum Machine Learning
items.summary: Quantum machine learning (QML) has emerged as a rapidly developing field at the intersection of quantum computing, artificial intelligence, and data science. As quantum hardware and algorithms continue to advance, there is a growing need for a rigorous and accessible text that explains how quantum principles can be used to design, analyze, and implement machine learning models.

items.title: Decoding sequence auditory expectations for clinical diagnostic and prognostic assessment of prolonged disorders of consciousness
items.summary: OBJECTIVE: Electroencephalogram (EEG) features are important objective markers for diagnostic and prognostic evaluation of prolonged disorders of consciousness (DOC). However, task-based EEG paradigms are limited by mismatches between task demands and patients' residual awareness, as well as the limited individual assessment capacity of machine-learning-based detection frameworks.

items.title: Ontology-constrained multi-LLM scoring of hypothesis support in the predictive processing literature
items.summary: Abstract Fragmentation is common in interdisciplinary fields with diverse methods and theoretical commitments. Predictive coding neuroscience is a clear example: its literature spans computational theory, electrophysiology, imaging, behavior, and modeling, creating a synthesis problem that conventional meta-analysis cannot easily resolve.

items.title: The Association Between Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease and Postoperative Delirium: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.summary: Background: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent and serious complication following surgery, particularly in high-risk patients such as those with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The relationship between COPD and the development of POD remains unclear, with existing studies providing inconsistent findings.

items.title: Digital engineering for quantum communication networks: A systematic review of models, simulators, and testbeds
items.summary: Research on quantum communication networks has grown rapidly in recent years, driven by progress in quantum devices, simulators, and experimental testbeds. As these systems become more complex, there is increasing interest in digital methods that can support analysis, prediction, and performance assessment without relying exclusively on physical experimentation.

items.title: Common phenomenal and neural substrate geometry in visual motion perception
items.summary: Abstract What is a possible physical substrate of the qualitative aspects of consciousness (qualia)? Answering this question is a central goal of consciousness research. Due to their subjective and ineffable nature, finding a quantitative way to characterise qualia from verbal description has thus far proven elusive.

items.summary: From William James's Transmission Theory to the Ben-Yehudah Transducer Model: Consciousness Beyond the Brain and the Question of Biological Reception This scientific, historical, and theoretical manuscript examines the relationship between William James's transmission hypothesis of consciousness and Yeshayahu Ben-Yehudah's independent investigation of SOURCE CONSCIOUSNESS, biological reception, and the Ben-Yehudah Transducer Model. The investigation begins with James's 1898 publication, Human Immortality: Two…

items.title: How many labels can a biological oscillator carry? A quality-factor screen for proposed information carriers
items.summary: How many distinguishable labels can a biological oscillator carry? Proposals invoking collective vibrational modes, endogenous electromagnetic fields, microtubule excitations and oscillatory phase codes are each debated on grounds particular to themselves, with no shared standard for comparison.

items.title: Practical limitations on robustness and scalability of quantum Internet
items.summary: Abstract The realization of a desirably functional quantum Internet is hindered by fundamental and practical challenges such as high loss during transmission of quantum systems, decoherence due to interaction with the environment, and fragility of quantum states under measurement. We study the implications of these constraints by analyzing the limitations on the scaling and robustness of the quantum Internet.

items.title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
items.summary: Designing protein sequences that satisfy both secondary structure requirements and solubility targets remains challenging. We present DiffSequence-Q, a hybrid multinomial diffusion model conditioned on secondary structure at each residue and a continuous solubility target.

items.title: Quantum Fourier integration of decay rates at next-to-leading order
items.summary: We discuss the use of quantum neural networks (QNNs) as a tool for integrating decay rates at next-to-leading order (NLO) in perturbation theory. Data-encoding quantum circuits admit a truncated Fourier-series representation, enabling a trained QNN to approximate a target integrand and provide the coefficients subsequently integrated with Quantum Fourier Iterative Amplitude Estimation (QFIAE).

items.title: Accelerating Quantum-Classical Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo with Shadow-Trained Neural Quantum States
items.summary: Quantum-classical auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (QC-AFQMC) uses a trial state prepared on a quantum computer to improve the accuracy of the classical AFQMC algorithm. State-of-the-art QC-AFQMC represents this state with matchgate shadows, so every trial-walker overlap and local energy must be averaged over many snapshots, making this classical computation a bottleneck.

items.title: Approaching quantum limits in sub-Rayleigh resolution using phase modulation optimization
items.summary: Spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) has made significant progress in incoherent optical imaging and has been implemented through various experimental approaches. Holography-based SPADE is widely used in proof-of-principle experiments because of its low cost, stable optical arrangement, and ease of implementation.

items.title: Higher-order topological quantum battery
items.summary: A quantum battery is a next-generation energy-storage device that exploits genuinely quantum properties such as superposition and coherence. We propose a second-order topological quantum battery coupled to a photonic crystal described by the breathing-Kagome model, where optical loss is present on all lattice sites while nonlinear gains are introduced selectively at the output sites.

items.title: Dithered Belief Propagation for Real-Time Quantum Memory Decoding
items.summary: We introduce dithered belief-propagation decoding for circuit-level quantum memory to mitigate the oscillations and trapping behavior that limit standard belief-propagation (BP) decoders for qLDPC codes. Our approach combines a quantum-adapted sign-flip mechanism with chained randomized prior perturbation.

items.title: Quantum machine learning for quantitative finance
items.summary: Abstract Machine learning (ML) and quantum ML (QML) have gained significant importance, as they offer powerful tools for tackling complex computational problems across various domains. An overview of QML’s uses in quantitative finance is presented here.

items.title: Parameter-Shift Rules for Gradients in Boson Sampling Experiments
items.summary: Abstract Using a robust photon loss model for photonic quantum experiments, we derive $n-$th order parameter-shift rules for computing gradients of Fock boson sampling transition probabilities where $n$ photons are sent into a lossy interferometer. We also show that one cannot naturally generalize this gradient recipe to the case of Gaussian boson sampling.

items.title: Time-Division Multiplexing: The Operational Rhythm and Temporal Organization Layer of Digital Life
items.summary: Continual agents must handle urgent interaction while retaining alternatives, replaying errors, and committing safe long-term changes. A previous digital-life framework distinguishes online (busy) and offline (idle) channels, but leaves open whether these are separate programs or phases of a common process and how their operations should be ordered.

items.summary: Optical coherence is a well-established branch of physical optics in which the statistical properties of fluctuating optical fields are described in terms of correlation functions over continuous spatial and temporal degrees of freedom (DoFs). Nevertheless, in any practical setting, only discrete DoFs are ever accessible.

items.title: Attention Renders Sensory Contents into Conscious State via Content-invariant Frontal-Posterior Coupling in Humans
items.summary: Abstract Although attention promotes conscious perception, how it does so remains unclear. Human neuroimaging research has richly characterized attentional modulation upon visual processing, yet it remains unclear which of its components act as precursors of consciousness, which constitute consciousness itself, and which merely reflect post-perceptual, response-related operations.

items.title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment
items.summary: Motor responses evoked by noxious stimulation are used to assess neurological function in hospitalized patients with disorders of consciousness. In standard bedside assessments, these stimuli are applied manually, resulting in substantial variation in force, duration, frequency, and location.

items.title: A systems-level energetic framework for conscious processing: energetic organization as a constraint on large-scale neural integration
items.summary: Conscious processing is associated with coordinated interactions among distributed neural systems, yet the biological constraints that enable and sustain large-scale neural integration remain incompletely understood. Contemporary theories emphasize computational, informational, and network mechanisms, while the potential contribution of systems-level energetic organization has received comparatively less explicit theoretical attention.

items.title: Probing chaos and criticality with observational entropy and finite-resolution measurements
items.summary: Coarse-grained measurements offer a scalable alternative to full state tomography for characterizing complex quantum dynamics. We show that observational entropy (OE), an information-theoretic entropy defined directly from finite-resolution measurement outcomes, provides a unified and experimentally accessible framework for quantifying chaos and probing criticality.

items.title: Quantum resources for everlasting communication security
items.summary: Abstract Quantum cryptography provides communication with everlasting security—a property unattainable by classical or post-quantum cryptography. Traditionally, quantum cryptography proclaims everlasting security by relying on principles such as no-cloning theorem, Bell inequalities, or the uncertainty principle, along with the standard assumption that legitimate users have no control over the communication channel.

items.title: The quantum-ready college: quantum technologies as an industry shift and how higher education should prepare
items.summary: Purpose This paper examines the emerging industry shift in which quantum technologies are evolving from isolated scientific breakthroughs into full-scale innovation ecosystems that will reshape higher education. Its purpose is to demonstrate why colleges must prepare now, well before fault tolerant quantum computers arrive, by developing quantum ready capacities across curriculum, workforce development, partnerships and cybersecurity.

items.title: Quantum Searching and Optimization Algorithms
items.summary: This book offers a rigorous and forward-looking exploration of one of the most consequential frontiers in modern computation: the use of quantum mechanics to accelerate search, optimization, learning, simulation, and secure information processing. It begins by establishing the conceptual and mathematical foundations of quantum computation, including quantum gates, circuit design, quantum parallelism, and the distinctions between classical and quantum models of information processing.

items.title: The Sociological Cogito and the Hard Problems of Science
items.summary: This groundbreaking work introduces the sociological cogito as a revolutionary paradigm for solving the most perplexing “hard problems” in science and philosophy: mathematics, logic, God, and consciousness. By challenging traditional Cartesian and Platonist approaches, it demonstrates how these seemingly transcendental phenomena are actually grounded in our social realities.

items.title: Everettian chance in no uncertain terms
items.summary: Abstract The current landscape of views on the role of chance in the Everett interpretation is rocky. Everettians (Wallace, 2012; Sebens and Carroll, 2018; McQueen and Vaidman, 2019) agree that chance values should be derived using rules of rationality governing agents’ uncertain reasoning and/or decision-making, but they cannot agree on how.

It is based on a linear-symmetry representation of atomic states using large-scale relativistic configuration interaction wavefunctions, and the quadrupole polarizabilities are obtained by a sum-over-states approach.

items.title: Autler-townes energy-level engineering for high-quality all-microwave qubit gate
items.summary: High-fidelity entangling gates are essential for realizing large-scale fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computing, yet existing approaches are limited: frequency-tuning techniques induce decoherence, while all-microwave-driven schemes suffer the trade-off between gate speed and leakage rate. Here, we introduce an energy-level engineering technique that employs the Autler-Townes effect to manipulate the nonlinearity of qubits without perturbing the computational subspace or degrading coherence time.

items.title: Elimination of quantum causal confusion in the presence of dual states
items.summary: There is a rich class of bipartite quantum correlations between qubits which are consistent both with measurements performed in parallel and measurements performed in sequence. This phenomenon has recently been termed \emph{quantum causal confusion}, which is made mathematically precise by the notion of a dual state---a bipartite density operator whose associated correlations are causally ambiguous.

items.title: Unitarity with respect to the clock of a dynamical local observer and the Einstein equivalence principle
items.summary: We investigate the unitarity of quantum evolution relative to an internal time defined by a local observer's clock. The observer is modeled as a relativistic particle carrying both a clock and a matter-field detector, analyzed first on a fixed curved background and subsequently within a fully diffeomorphism-invariant theory of dynamical gravity.

However, their safety, feasibility, and optimal adaptation remain uncertain in patients with neurodegenerative disorders (NDDs), particularly those with dementia and Parkinson’s disease.

items.title: The Hard Problem of Consciousness and Qualia in the Acta Universi Hypothesis
items.summary: The Hard Problem of Consciousness and Qualia in the Acta Universi Hypothesis Abstract (EN) The hard problem of consciousness asks why physical processes are accompanied by subjective experience. items.title: A glutamatergic projection from the central medial thalamic nucleus to the red nucleus regulates states of consciousness during sevoflurane anesthesia in mice
items.summary: General anesthetics like sevoflurane are clinically essential, yet the neural circuits governing their induction of unconsciousness and recovery remain incompletely defined. Here, we show the potential involvement of the vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (Vglut2)-expressing glutamatergic neurons in the central medial thalamus (CMT Vglut2 neurons) in modulation states of consciousness under sevoflurane anesthesia.

items.title: From unimodal to multimodal deep physiological signal analysis in healthcare: A survey of models, fusion and explainability
items.summary: Physiological signal analysis supports objective assessment of emotion, stress, pain, and disease progression in healthcare systems. Early research focused mainly on unimodal signals, which perform well in controlled settings but are often affected by noise, limited contextual information and reduced generalisability.

items.title: Patient-specific factors are associated with distinct brain network connectivity in disorders of consciousness
items.summary: Disorders of consciousness (DoC) arise from diverse etiologies and exhibit substantial clinical heterogeneity, including variations in patient age and time since injury. However, how these clinical characteristics relate to large-scale brain network connectivity and are associated with consciousness levels and functional outcomes remains poorly understood.

items.title: Operationally induced preferred basis in unitary quantum mechanics
items.summary: Abstract The preferred-basis problem remains under unitary system--apparatus dynamics, whereas measurements have mutually exclusive outcomes. The present framework places basis selection in the complete preparation--measurement arrangement.

items.title: Universal quantum gate set for multimode Schrödinger cat states stabilized by nonlocal dissipation engineering
items.summary: Schrödinger cat states provide a hardware-efficient platform for bosonic quantum error correction by encoding logical information in protected manifolds of harmonic oscillators. While previous work has demonstrated the dissipative stabilization of multi-mode Schrödinger cat states as robust quantum memories, a framework for universal quantum computation has remained unavailable.

items.summary: General anesthesia has long been understood as a unitary phenomenon driven by neural suppression — a reduction in cortical activity, entropy, and complexity that renders the brain unable to sustain conscious processing. Yet two structurally and pharmacologically distinct compounds, N,N-Dimethyltryptamine (DMT) and ketamine, produce clinical unresponsiveness while maintaining or increasing cortical complexity, a pattern fundamentally incompatible with the suppression paradigm.

items.summary: Abstract Benchmarking quantum processors is a central task in every roadmap aimed at quantum advantage. Here, we discuss a benchmarking protocol based on the violation of the Svetlichny inequality, which is designed to simulate genuine multipartite nonlocality.

items.title: Qualia Is Not a Pseudoproblem: A Response to Balconi et al. (2026), 'The End of Qualia'
items.summary: A response to Balconi et al.'s (2026) Frontiers in Psychology editorial proposing that qualia be retired as a pseudoproblem in Kuhn's sense. The letter argues that the collection the editorial introduces does not support its eliminative frame; that a malformed question has never licensed abandoning the phenomenon it names; and that first-person report remains the foundation on which pain science, affective neuroscience, and clinical measurement were built — the reports came first, and the instruments followed them.

items.title: Adaptive sensing beyond non-adaptive information limits: End-to-end co-design of geometry, policy, and inference
items.summary: Inverse design has transformed vast physical parameter spaces into a substrate for emergent functionality, raising the tantalizing prospect of relocating intelligence from the digital domain into the physical world itself. Nowhere is this prospect more consequential than in sensing, where the analog-to-digital interface imposes a fundamental bottleneck: information not captured by the hardware is irrevocably lost to any downstream algorithm.

items.summary: Superconducting quantum circuits are among the most promising platforms for quantum computing, but their design remains a complex inverse problem, requiring the identification of circuit architectures and physical parameters capable of reproducing a desired quantum response. Existing approaches mainly rely on iterative optimization, predefined topologies, or previously simulated device families, limiting their flexibility as circuit complexity increases.

items.title: Human consciousness versus the scientific method
items.summary: This study explores how science has approached the complex phenomenon of human consciousness, emphasizing the challenges of addressing subjectivity through objective and replicable methodologies. A bibliometric analysis was conducted using the Scopus database, identifying 1,143 documents between 1990 and 2024.

items.title: Minimal and Moderate Sedation Agents
items.summary: Sedation refers to a medically induced alteration in consciousness intended to reduce anxiety, promote relaxation, and facilitate patient cooperation. This chapter focuses on the pharmacologic agents most commonly used in minimal and moderate pediatric dental sedation.

items.title: Reliable Entropy Estimation from Observed Statistics for Device-Independent Quantum Cryptography
items.summary: We introduce a numerical framework for reliably estimating conditional von Neumann entropies, a central quantity in device-independent quantum cryptography and randomness generation. Our method is based on semidefinite relaxations derived from the Navascués--Pironio--Acín hierarchy and provides entropy bounds directly from observed statistics, assuming only the validity of quantum mechanics.

items.title: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems
items.summary: Knowledge distillation transfers predictions, representations, or other supervisory information between learning models and is increasingly investigated in quantum machine learning. Its applications extend beyond compression to cross-architecture transfer, circuit approximation, distributed learning, and classical deployment of models trained using quantum-derived supervision.

items.title: Room-Temperature Quantum Emission from Boron Nitride Nanotubes
items.summary: Quantum information systems such as quantum key distribution and quantum communications require bright, high-purity, stable sources of single photons to act as carriers of quantum information. As such, methods for obtaining single photon emitters (SPEs) in solid-state devices capable of articulating with quantum photonic circuits are a necessary obstacle that must be overcome.

items.title: Dynamical effects induced by synthetic SU(1,1) gauge fields
items.summary: Compact gauge fields are powerful tools for controlling quantum dynamics and topological phases of matter. Non-compact gauge fields are particularly relevant for open systems, where particles or energy are exchanged with the environment.

items.title: Polynomial-time classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss
items.summary: Sampling experiments are a leading approach to demonstrating quantum computational advantage, yet their robustness to experimental noise is not completely understood. We develop a common framework for classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss, including pure loss.

items.title: Quantum enhanced beam displacement estimation: sensitivity limits, optimal probes, and measurement schemes
items.summary: We investigate the ultimate sensitivity limits for measuring small transverse beam displacements and identify optimal strategies that attain them, using the framework of mode parameter estimation. We contrast two families of states with different resource constraints, using Hermite-Gauss and Laguerre-Gauss mode pairs.

items.title: Disorder-blind Mpemba acceleration of quantum state preparation
items.summary: Using the strong Mpemba effect to accelerate relaxation by initial-state design requires suppressing the slowest mode, which typically needs prior knowledge of the system. However, in disordered systems, this mode is sample-dependent, so a fixed preparation generally retains a slow-mode overlap.

items.title: Recalibration-Aware Optimization of ZEFOZ Operating Points in $^{167}\mathrm{Er}^{3+}:\mathrm{Y}_2\mathrm{SiO}_5$ for Quantum Memories
items.summary: Erbium-doped solids like $^{167}\mathrm{Er}^{3+}:\mathrm{Y}_2\mathrm{SiO}_5$ have properties that make them suitable for quantum-network memories, however, their unquenched effective electronic spin causes rapid magnetic decoherence. Operating at Zero First-Order Zeeman (ZEFOZ) points allows us to mitigate this, where we evaluate the ZEFOZ landscape for Site-2 $^{167}\mathrm{Er}^{3+}$ by incorporating a full-Hessian spin-Hamiltonian treatment with the anisotropic magnetic-field covariance derived from the native…

items.title: Asymptotic analysis of the dynamical field-field correlation function of the impenetrable Bose gas
items.summary: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotic behaviour of the two-point correlation function of fields of the impenetrable Bose gas in equilibrium states characterized by a quasi-momentum distribution (or filling fraction). This includes, in particular, the cases of Gibbs and generalized Gibbs ensembles.

items.title: Testing Gravitationally-Induced-Entanglement with Massive Particles and Quantum Clocks
items.summary: We present an experimental proposal to test whether gravity can entangle a levitated particle with an array of quantum clocks. By harnessing the collective interaction between a micrometer-scale particle and an array of ultra-precise nuclear clocks, our scheme offers a conceivable path to observing gravitationally mediated entanglement with quantum clocks in the laboratory.

items.title: Recovery gates as a resource in repetition-code process tomography: exhaustive gate-optimal designs for three, five and seven qubits
items.summary: Process tomography built on stabilizer codes compares the logical channel of a repetition code with a reference channel, and the decoder that produces that channel is almost always fixed to the standard minimum-weight one. We ask how many physical single-qubit Pauli gates the decoder actually needs when the measurement basis is fixed---the constraint under which the count is a resource rather than a bookkeeping artefact.

items.title: Beyond Quantum Messages: Toward Quantum-Native Network Functioning
items.summary: The Quantum Internet is commonly envisioned as a network that transports quantum states and distributes entanglement as the key resource underpinning distributed quantum applications. This view is necessary but incomplete if quantum phenomena are confined to what the network carries or manages, while network functionalities remain grounded predominantly in classical abstractions.

items.title: Dualities in one-dimensional quantum lattice models: Lie groups, Schur-Weyl duality and symmetry breaking
items.summary: We present a systematic framework for gauging continuous symmetries, and show that the Schur-Weyl duality arises naturally as a realization of this construction with open boundary conditions. Restricting to compact Lie group symmetries, we construct dual models for one-dimensional quantum lattice models exhibiting those symmetries.

items.title: Entropic measures of quantum information
items.summary: Entropy has played a pivotal role in physics ever since its inception by Clausius in the early industrial age. Shannon ushered the concept into the information age by using it to describe fundamental limits of information processing, founding the field of information theory.

items.title: Certifying quantum code and circuit distances at scale
items.summary: Code and circuit distances characterize how strongly quantum error correction suppresses logical errors and guide code comparisons, schedule choices and resource estimates. Yet many published distances are only upper bounds from heuristic searches.

items.title: Finite-Time Thermodynamic Routing in an Anharmonic Collective Quantum Otto Engine
items.summary: The Gibbs state determined by a thermal reservoir does not determine how a working medium approaches it or how fluctuations accumulate over repeated cycles. We exploit this kinetic freedom in an anharmonic collective quantum Otto engine.

items.title: Persistent level-resolved transmon population after dispersive readout, and the limits of its open-system description
items.summary: We calculate the level-resolved transmon population remaining after dispersive readout with a converged open-system model. The drive and qubit-cavity coupling use the rotating-wave approximation, while the cavity is a quantized mode in a frame displaced by its classical trajectory.

items.title: Optimal finite-copy readout of three-qubit entanglement with state retention
items.summary: For unknown three-qubit pure states, we characterize the optimal trade-off among GHZ-class certification, binary probability readout of the three-tangle, and conditional state retention. The vanishing ideal of the null class specifies the optimal certification subspace, while a polynomial multiplication operator gives the spectral limit for binary readout.

items.title: QDiff: Differential Testing of Quantum Software Stacks
items.summary: Over the past few years, several quantum software stacks (QSS) have been developed in response to rapid hardware advances in quantum computing. A QSS includes a quantum programming language, an optimizing compiler that translates a quantum algorithm written in a high-level language into quantum gate instructions, a quantum simulator that emulates these instructions on a classical device, and a software controller that sends analog signals to a very expensive quantum hardware based on quantum circuits.

items.title: Quantum Advantage with Sign-Free Proofs: An Oracle Separation between $\mathsf{StoqMA}$ and $\mathsf{MA}$
items.summary: Several landmark oracle results (FOCS 2000, FOCS 2025, STOC 2026) establish strict separations along the chain $\mathsf{MA} \subseteq \mathsf{QCMA} \subseteq \mathsf{QMA}$, showing that quantum verification and quantum witnesses can each provide additional power over classical proof systems. These separations, however, use substantial coherent quantum computation, often through the quantum Fourier transform.

items.title: Coherent phase slips in coupled rings: from weak to strong interactions
items.summary: We study the coherent transfer of circulation between two weakly coupled lattice rings of ultracold bosons, in which a persistent current initially prepared in one ring oscillates back and forth between the rings without net transfer of particles. Combining Bose--Hubbard simulations with their Gross--Pitaevskii and quantum phase model limits, we show that similar current oscillations arise from two distinct microscopic mechanisms.

items.title: Primitive Quantum Gates for an $SU(3)$ Discrete Subgroup: $Σ(216\times3)$
items.summary: We construct a primitive gate set for the digital quantum simulation of the $648$-element discrete subgroup of $SU(3)$, $\dsb$. The five algorithmic primitives are the inversion, group multiplication, trace, group Fourier transform, and kinetic-phase gates, for which we provide qubit and qutrit--qubit decompositions.

items.title: Non-Unitary Quantum Butterfly Effect: Theory and Experiment
items.summary: We present a generalization of the out of time order correlator (OTOC) for non-unitary systems. For a Haar-random brickwork qudit-circuit, peppered with local, projective measurement, we calculate the infinite-temperature, ensemble-average OTOC.

items.title: Machine learning quantum data to accelerate quantum Monte Carlo
items.summary: Simulating strongly correlated electrons in molecules and materials remains a central goal for quantum computing. A promising strategy uses quantum processors to prepare trial wavefunctions that guide classical quantum Monte Carlo (QMC).

items.title: Semi-Analytical Geometric Synthesis of Robust Quantum Controls
items.summary: High-fidelity quantum gates are a central requirement for fault-tolerant quantum computation, yet their implementation is limited by the sensitivity of qubits to environmental noise and by control non-idealities. To mitigate these effects, quantum gates can be designed as dynamically corrected gates (DCGs), where control sequences are engineered to suppress the impact of errors on the resulting operation.

items.title: Quantum trajectory of a spin oscillator, continuous retrodiction beyond the Heisenberg uncertainty relation
items.summary: The Heisenberg uncertainty relation in quantum mechanics limits the precision of predicting the outcome of measurements of any non-commuting observables. However, this restriction does not apply to retrodictive guessing of the outcomes of past measurements.

items.title: Nonuniform Time-bins for Making Raw QRNG Outputs Uniform
items.summary: Random numbers play a vital role in scientific simulations and cryptography. Both randomness and security are critical requirements for random number generators (RNGs). However, classical RNGs often rely on mathematical assumptions that can compromise security, while quantum RNGs (QRNGs) face challenges, including non-uniform output due to the lack of specialized single-photon sources.

items.title: Exponential mixing time for the Davies dynamics of the quantum random energy model
items.summary: We prove exponentially slow thermalization for the quantum random energy model (QREM) under Davies dynamics. The QREM is the $n$-qubit Hamiltonian $H=ΓT+U$, where $U$ assigns independent Gaussian energies with variance equal to the system size to computational-basis configurations and $T$ is the transverse field generated by single-qubit Pauli $X$ operators.

items.title: Effective Thermodynamics of a Volume-Dependent Qubit
items.summary: We develop an effective thermodynamics for a qubit whose energy gap depends inversely on a volume-like control parameter, $Δ(V)=Δ_0/V$, where $V$ is a spectral-control coordinate rather than a literal mechanical volume. Starting from the canonical Gibbs state, we derive a complete thermodynamic structure from the Helmholtz potential and its Legendre and stability properties, including the fundamental relation $S(U,V)$, a generalized pressure conjugate to $V$, the equation of state $U=PV$, the first law, and the…

items.title: From maximum work to maximum power in an optimally controlled quantum Ising Otto engine
items.summary: In finite-time quantum Otto engines, maximizing power requires balancing the duration of the unitary strokes against the losses from nonadiabatic excitations. We address this trade-off in an Otto engine with a free-fermion working medium, using quantum optimal control.

items.title: Quantum transport of vortex electrons in bending magnets and circular accelerators
items.summary: Controlling the sizes and phase structure of single-particle wave packets in accelerators remains an experimental challenge and requires understanding how bending magnets transform these states. An important example is transporting relativistic vortex electrons through the magnets to a collision point while keeping a narrow orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) distribution.

items.title: Crosstalk-Induced Row Hammer Attacks on Quantum Random Access Codes
items.summary: Quantum processors remain susceptible to crosstalk-induced effects despite the continuous evolution of their underlying hardware architectures. In this work, we experimentally investigate the effectiveness of crosstalk-induced attacks across six IBM superconducting quantum processors and one IQM processor.

items.title: Monopoles, Scattering and Generalized Symmetries on a Quantum Computer
items.summary: Quantum computers have advanced to the stage that interesting many-body quantum phenomena can be observed. A striking example is the magnetic monopole paradox, a problem that was only solved recently using the language of generalized symmetries.

items.title: Negative non-linear differential dissipation in mechanical quartz resonators
items.summary: We observe negative non-linear differential dissipation in a low-frequency (32.7 kHz) miniature quartz tuning fork, representing a high-Q piezoelectric resonator, at temperatures below 0.3 K. Similar drive-induced dissipation suppression has previously been reported in superconducting microwave resonators, and high-frequency MEMS devices, associated to coupling with tunneling two-level systems (TTLSs).

items.title: Continuous variable payload transmitter for the SPOQC mission
items.summary: The continuous variable (CV) quantum key distribution (QKD) scheme enables two parties to share a secret key separated by a certain distance. Here we propose, design, build, test and show results of a CV payload transmitter, intended to demonstrate downlink based QKD from a CubeSat in low earth orbit.

items.title: Multirobust Control Pulses Designed by Iterative Quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser Algorithm
items.summary: We introduce a multi-robust quantum control strategy designed to suppress multilevel leakage outside the computational qubit space while simultaneously ensuring robustness against unknown inhomogeneities in control parameters. It is based on a reformulation of the Derivative Removal by Adiabatic Gate (DRAG) technique which allows for the full incorporation of control pulses originally designed for two-level models by using the iterative quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser (KAM) algorithm.

items.title: Constrained Quantum Imaginary Time in Krylov Space
items.summary: We introduce constrained quantum imaginary time evolution (CQITE), extending quantum imaginary time evolution (QITE) to constrained-search dynamics for ground-state preparation with prescribed expectation-value constraints. A central challenge in practical QITE is constructing a compact unitary representation of the imaginary-time evolution while maintaining accuracy and controlling the approximation error.

items.title: Discrete quadrature spectrum of composite bosons: Weyl relation, intensity correlations, and binned homodyne detection
items.summary: A composite boson made of two fermions can look elementary under one measurement and composite under another. In an exactly solvable paired-mode model we compare three probes: classical drives, periodically binned quadrature statistics, and intensity correlations $g^{(2)}$.

items.title: Development of time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy using heralded emission spectroscopy for organic light-emitting materials
items.summary: Organic light-emitting materials are widely used in optoelectronics and bioimaging, but sometimes conventional fluorescence spectroscopy techniques can be limited by scattering, background fluorescence, photon pile-up and photobleaching. We report a quantum-spectroscopic approach using frequency-entangled, nondegenerate photon pairs generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion with heralded detection, to perform photoluminescence lifetime measurements at low excitation intensities.

items.title: Detecting Nonbilocal Correlations via Parameterized Elegant Joint Measurement
items.summary: Quantum networks constitute a defining resource for quantum information processing; however, their nonclassical behavior is jointly governed by the choice of measurement basis and the independence of the distributed sources. We study a bilocal entanglement-swapping network in which the central node performs a three-parameter elegant joint measurement (EJM).

items.title: Observation of Inter-Transition Interference
items.summary: Many well-known quantum interference phenomena are associated with coherent superpositions of quantum states. Recent theoretical work showed that dissipative coupling between transition coherences can give rise to a distinct form of quantum interference in open quantum systems, termed inter-transition interference (ITI).

items.title: Efficient preparation of spin-squeezed states with Grover's algorithm
items.summary: We propose a scheme for preparing spin-squeezed states in an ensemble of $N$ spin-$1/2$ particles based on Grover's algorithm. With only a few oracles, the scheme can exactly prepare superpositions of a few neighboring Dicke states with the Wineland squeezing parameter scaling as $N^{-1}$.

items.title: Separability and lower bounds of concurrence via symmetric measurement correlations
items.summary: The detection and quantification of quantum entanglement is a central issue in quantum information science, particularly for unknown quantum states. Based on symmetric measurement correlation matrices, we present a family of separability criteria that can be experimentally applied without state tomography, and recover some related existing criteria as special cases.

items.title: Universal Phase Locking from Slowly Varying Inhomogeneity in Tunnel-Coupled One-Dimensional Condensates
items.summary: The sine-Gordon model can be experimentally realised by tunnel-coupled one-dimensional Bose condensates. However, the experiments show relaxation to a phase-locked state, which conflicts with the predictions of the homogeneous integrable theory.

items.title: Majorana corner modes and tunable braiding in an altermagnet-superconductor heterostructure
items.summary: Zeeman fields are usually required for realizing and manipulating Majorana corner modes at the cost of suppressed superconducting pairing. Altermagnetism offers a new route toward realizing Majorana corner modes under zero net external magnetic fields.

items.title: Observing mixed-state Uhlmann winding numbers in integrated photonic quantum walks
items.summary: Integer winding numbers provide a well-established classification of topological phases protected by chiral symmetry at zero temperature, but extending this classification to thermal mixed states remains challenging. The Uhlmann phase, a mixed-state extension of the Berry phase, provides a geometric framework for characterizing finite-temperature topology.

items.title: Optimal quantum metrology with restricted controls
items.summary: Quantum control can enhance sensing precision, but practical protocols are constrained by probe preparation and the available control resources. Optimizing the sensing protocol within these constraints helps establish what precision is experimentally attainable.

items.title: Efficient Pauli Truncation from Operator Stabilizer Rényi Entropy
items.summary: Operator stabilizer Rényi entropy (OSE) quantifies the magic of Heisenberg operators and serves as a diagnostic of their compressibility in the Pauli basis. We establish rigorous bounds showing when an operator can be efficiently approximated by Pauli truncation in terms of the scaling of its OSE.

items.title: Information-Spectrum General Formulas for the Capacity Region of Classical-Quantum Multiple Access Channels
items.summary: For classical-quantum multiple access channels (cq-MACs) with two senders, we give several general expressions for the capacity region, valid for arbitrary sequences of channels. In the case of asymptotically vanishing error ($\varepsilon=0$), the capacity region is expressed in terms of spectral inf-mutual information rates.

items.title: Probing Non-Abelian Topology through Quench Dynamics
items.summary: Quench dynamics offer valuable insights to topological matter, wherein the emergent topological phenomena serve as a dynamic probe to the topology of static Hamiltonians. While such a practice has been widely applied to detect the Abelian band topology or the Euler-class topology of band nodes, little is known regarding the quench dynamics of non-Abelian topological insulators in multiband systems, where the intertwining geometry of all eigenstates necessitates the description of noncommutative topological charges.

items.title: Bell Test and Quantum State-Space Geometry
items.summary: We explore a minimal phenomenological model of coupling between the geometry of the classical spacetime and the quantum state space. Assuming a simple structure of the combined manifold, bilinear interaction between the corresponding geometric scalars and the simplest case of the two-qubit entanglement dynamics, we derive an illustrative upper bound on the geometric coupling constant from the requirement of the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality violation over a finite time interval.

items.title: Demystifying Graviton Detection
items.summary: Detecting single gravitons is possible through the extraction of discrete energy quanta from passing gravitational waves. For decades, this was considered hopeless, with estimates suggesting a detector the size of Jupiter.

items.title: Information flow control in hybrid quantum networks
items.summary: Quantum resources can change the dynamical features and operational behaviors of conventional networks. Long-distance entanglement supports information transfer between nodes lacking a direct connection.

items.title: Structured Quantum Hardness from Unstructured Assumptions
items.summary: Whether useful structured hardness can arise from unstructured assumptions is a fundamental question in complexity and cryptography. The longstanding Bennett-Gill question asks whether $\mathsf{NP}\cap\mathsf{coNP}$ remains hard relative to a random oracle; [GIKKLS, STOC 2023] recently gave a conditional affirmative answer in the classical setting.

items.title: Weak Values in Postselected Quantum Trajectories
items.summary: Weak value (WV) describes the amplified response of a meter when the measured system undergoes postselection. While conventional WV theory mainly rests on a single system-meter interaction setting, it remains unexplored whether WV can act as an effective pointer for sequential quantum measurements under postselection.

items.title: Extensions of the Haldane gap proof: higher dimensions, near degeneracy, fermions and tensor-network states
items.summary: A recent remarkable paper by OpenAI showed that the spin-one Heisenberg chain with periodic boundary conditions has a spectral gap in the thermodynamic limit. The proof elegantly deduces this gap from the Hamiltonian's spectrum on a finite system.

items.title: Certifying the Rydberg-exposure limit of a globally driven controlled-Z gate
items.summary: Rydberg excitation enables entangling gates in neutral-atom quantum processors but also exposes them to spontaneous decay. Whether this exposure can be made arbitrarily small through pulse shaping and longer gate times has remained unresolved.

items.title: Spin-Exchange-Controlled Nonclassical Light in Cavity Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
items.summary: Controlling nonclassical light while maintaining a finite cavity response requires selective suppression of unwanted multiphoton excitation. We investigate a ring-cavity system containing two three-level emitters coupled by a coherent spin-exchange interaction, where electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) provides resonant access to a dark-state polariton.

items.title: Operational Characterizations and Resource Structure of the Interactive Weight of Quantum Instruments
items.summary: Quantifying the interactivity of quantum instruments is fundamental to understanding their resource structure and operational capabilities. Here, we introduce the interactive weight of quantum instruments as a resource quantifier that measures the minimum fraction of an instrument that cannot be explained by non-interactive components.

items.title: Observable-Based Learning of Effective Entanglement Hamiltonians
items.summary: Determining the entanglement Hamiltonian (EH) of an interacting quantum many-body system remains a fundamental challenge beyond special analytically tractable cases. Here we develop an observable-matching framework for learning effective EHs, which we demonstrate using response estimates from quantum Monte Carlo.

items.title: Fidelity Determines the Minimum Error of Quantum Recovery
items.summary: Even a recovery that maximizes worst-input entanglement fidelity can retain avoidable errors in subsequent measurements. Entanglement fidelity is the probability of passing a test of whether the state and its entanglement were preserved; infidelity is the probability of failing it.

items.title: Frustration-freeness is decidable but unprovable
items.summary: The frustration-free property is valuable in quantum many-body systems, which states that its ground states simultaneously minimize all local interaction terms, even when these terms act on overlapping degrees of freedom. Prominent examples include the AKLT model and Kitaev's toric code model, which serve as paradigmatic models of symmetry-protected topological phases and topological order, respectively.

items.title: Asymptotic advantage of quantum one-way and SMP communication for total functions
items.summary: We exhibit a total Boolean function on n input bits whose bounded-error quantum simultaneous-message (and hence one-way) communication complexity is in O(\sqrt n), whereas its randomised one-way (and hence simultaneous-message) communication complexity is in Ω(n). The same function admits a classical simultaneous-message protocol of cost O(\sqrt n) when the players share O(\sqrt n) EPR pairs.

items.title: Quantum simulation of classical RCL circuits via complexification and Schrödingerization
items.summary: The decomplexification procedure establishes a mathematical equivalence between finite dimensional quantum dynamics and classical dynamics by mapping the complex quantum domain onto the real classical one. Its inverse process, complexification --- which lifts a classical dynamics to an equivalent quantum formulation --- is of great interest, particularly because it enables the quantum simulation of equations that are of classical relevance.

items.title: Unifying First-Order Coherence, Concurrence, and Bell Correlations in Three-Flavor Neutrino Oscillations
items.summary: Neutrino oscillations provide a natural setting for investigating the quantum character of flavor conversion and the distribution of quantum resources over macroscopic distances. Here, we study exact relations among purity-based first-order coherence, pairwise concurrence, and the maximal Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) value in coherent three-flavor neutrino oscillations.

items.title: Upper and lower bounds for few-copy Gaussian tomography, and the absence of a fermionic warm regime
items.summary: Chen, Mele, Mele and Preskill proved a crossover for bosonic Gaussian tomography: cold states need $Θ(m^3/ε^2)$ copies under single-copy or few-copy measurements, warm ones $Θ(m^2/ε^2)$. The author proved $Ω(m^3/ε^2)$ for adaptive single-copy tomography of mixed fermionic Gaussian states.

items.summary: The free particle is the most elementary dynamical system in quantum mechanics. Despite remarkable progress in quantum control of increasingly massive solid-state mechanical oscillators, the analogous control of the free-particle counterpart has remained elusive.

items.title: Managing Emerging Technologies for Financial Transformation: An Integrative TAM–DOI–RBV Framework
items.summary: Advances in quantum computing and AR/VR are transforming financial management and consumer interactions, yet their integration continues to face challenges related to adoption, security, and organizational readiness. This study aims to analyze the integration of these technologies into financial management and examine their implications for organizational purpose, financial management strategies, and consumer behavior.

items.title: Almost-Quantum Correlations Violate Information Causality
items.summary: Information causality (IC) posits that communicating m classical bits cannot give the receiver access to more than m bits of information about the sender's independent data. Although IC holds in quantum theory and excludes a broad class of supra-quantum correlations, its validity for the almost-quantum set has remained open.

items.title: Ageing and anaesthetic sensitivity: the role of inflammaging in the vulnerable surgical brain
items.summary: Ageing surgical patients demonstrate increased vulnerability to anaesthetic agents, including heightened sensitivity, reduced drug requirements, and delayed emergence, and they are also at increased risk of postoperative complications such as delirium and haemodynamic instability. These phenomena are only partially understood and have traditionally been attributed to the global functional decline associated with ageing.

items.summary: Heat generation limits computation, classical and quantum, from single logic gates to entire data centers. However, an in principle limiting physical factor can sometimes be turned into a resource.

items.title: Scalable Transpilation for Overcoming Restricted Connectivity in Distributed Superconducting Quantum Architectures
items.summary: Distributed Quantum Computing (DQC) offers a promising pathway to scale superconducting quantum hardware, but restricted inter- and intra-module connectivity creates a major transpilation bottleneck. Current DQC transpilation methods often assume idealized hardware connectivity, ignore subsequent intra-module routing, or suffer from substantial computational overheads that limit their applicability at scale.

items.title: Improving Gravitationally Induced Entanglement in Interferometric Configurations
items.summary: Proposals to detect gravitationally induced entanglement between massive particles offer a promising pathway toward probing the quantum nature of gravity. We perform a systematic geometric optimization and comparative analysis of Stern--Gerlach (SG) and Mach--Zehnder (MZ) matter-wave interferometers for this purpose, deriving exact analytical expressions for the gravitational phase of each configuration.

items.title: Nonequilibrium Spin-Glass Order in a Long-Range Quantum Ising Glass and Its Sensitivity to Noise
items.summary: We study spin-glass order after a transverse-field quench in a long-range quantum Ising glass. The diagonal-ensemble Edwards-Anderson order coincides at the no-quench and zero-field endpoints, yet in between cold shells overshoot it and hot shells undershoot it.

items.title: High-fidelity CNOT gates in photonic integrated circuits using composite segmented directional couplers
items.summary: Directional couplers are fundamental building blocks for integrated quantum photonic circuits but are highly sensitive to fabrication imperfections. We demonstrate that composite segmented directional couplers (CSDCs) enhance gate fidelity without active tuning.

items.title: Advanced meteorological modeling framework integrating quantum computing and machine learning for hurricane track prediction beyond traditional forecasting limitations
items.summary: Introduction Accurate prediction of hurricane tracks, intensity, and rapid intensification remains a major challenge in meteorological forecasting. This study investigates whether a hybrid quantum-classical approach, called the Quantum-Enhanced Neural Network (QENN), can improve tropical cyclone prediction.

items.title: Quantum machine learning: A comprehensive survey of models, tools, and challenges
items.summary: Abstract Quantum Machine Learning (QML) is an emerging interdisciplinary field that merges quantum computing with classical machine learning (ML) to enhance computational efficiency, scalability, and accuracy in data-driven tasks. By leveraging quantum properties such as superposition, entanglement, and quantum parallelism, QML has the potential to solve complex problems that are intractable for classical models.

items.title: The Reference System Loophole
items.summary: I argue that the Extended Wigner's Friend theorems have a `loophole' that has previously not been appreciated, coming from the fact that we typically need a reference system to give meaning to a measurement outcome. I show how this loophole can be used in the context of the Local Friendliness theorem to preserve the predictions of quantum mechanics without denying Local Friendliness, and I respond to some objections.

items.title: Quantum adversarial physics as a red team framework for physical-layer attacks on quantum cryptographic systems
items.summary: Abstract This paper presents a formal adversarial methodology, Quantum Adversarial Physics (QAP), for red teaming quantum communication systems, with a focus on Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and related quantum protocols. Rather than treating quantum mechanical principles as immutable security guarantees, QAP operationalises them as adversarial variables: coherence times, entanglement correlations, and entropy flows are each reframed as exploitable attack surfaces.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Classical vs Quantum Secret Sharing Schemes
items.summary: The fundamental concepts, safety guarantees, efficiency, and applicability to real-world cryptographic applications of both classical and quantum secret sharing techniques are carefully discussed in this work. Shamir’s and Blakley’s schemes are examples of CSS schemes that for long have provided information-theoretic security for sharing secrets among multiple parties such that only authorized subsets are able to retrieve the secret.

items.title: Negative quasiprobability trajectories for Bell-diagonal states under local decoherence
items.summary: The fluctuation theorem (FT) relates microscopic trajectory distributions to macroscopic averages. Using quasiprobability trajectories, this framework has recently been extended to quantum information dynamics.

items.title: Quantum Machine Learning in Medical Imaging: A Primer for Radiologists
items.summary: Deep learning has transformed radiology, but the computational cost of training and deploying modern models is outpacing what classical hardware can support. Quantum computing has been proposed as one response to this bottleneck: an n-qubit system can represent $2^n$ states simultaneously, although practical speedups require efficient algorithms, data encoding, and measurement strategies rather than superposition alone.

items.title: From Quantum Cryptography to Intuitionism and Beyond: Relativity, Many-Worlds and Non-Locality
items.summary: After a recollection of some of my encounters with Gilles Brassard, on the occasion of his 70th birthday I present, first, a new idea on the creation of new information at a limited rate. Next, I develop the idea that “indeterminacy is relative” and how this illuminates the compatibility between relativity and non-locality.

items.title: Inferring brain structural complexity from dynamical measures
items.summary: Complexity, commonly defined as the coexistence of integration and differentiation, is a fundamental property of thalamocortical networks and is regarded as a prerequisite for adaptive brain function and consciousness. A variety of metrics have been developed to estimate neural complexity from recorded activity and are increasingly employed in both research and clinical settings.

items.title: EL-RAKHAWI TOPOLOGICAL-PHENOMENAL CONSCIOUSNESS RESONANCE SYSTEM (TPCRS) An Objective, Mathematically Closed Framework for Mapping and Quantifying Subjective Experience via Causal Neural Geometry
items.summary: The El-Rakhawi Topological-Phenomenal Consciousness Resonance System (TPCRS) addresses the "Hard Problem of Consciousness" by providing the first mathematically closed framework for objectively quantifying subjective experience. Current neuroscience relies on unreliable behavioral assessments or statistical correlations that cannot distinguish conscious awareness from unconscious processing.

items.title: Quantum Watermarking: A Comprehensive Review of Principles, Challenges, and Future Prospects
items.summary: Quantum Watermarking (QWM) is an emerging field that combines quantum information theory with digital watermarking techniques to enhance the security of digital content. By leveraging quantum properties such as superposition, entanglement, and the no-cloning theorem, QWM provides robust protection against unauthorised access, tampering, and duplication—offering a significant advantage over classical methods.

items.title: The medium is the message: How neurometabolic entanglement generates conscious experience
items.summary: Most neuroscientific accounts of consciousness assume that conscious experience is constituted by the information conveyed between neurons. The physical-chemical details of the metabolic and physiological processes that convey this information are correspondingly presumed to be relevant only insofar as they support the organization of information processes.

items.title: The Composite Architecture of Time: Temporal Unity, Relational Compatibility, and the Emergence of a Classical Temporal World
items.summary: Physics provides several rigorous temporal structures without requiring them to collapse into a single, observer-independent time variable. Quantum dynamics can be conditioned on internal clocks; relativity supplies local proper times and causal relations; decoherence can make probabilities for selected histories approximately autonomous; records make parts of those histories accessible; and statistical mechanics accounts for macroscopic temporal orientation under suitable boundary conditions.

items.title: Quantum Integrated High-Performance Computing: Envisioning a layered architecture for next-generation hybrid computing infrastructure
items.summary: High-performance computing (HPC) has evolved over decades through multiple architectural transitions, from vector supercomputers to massively parallel CPU clusters and GPU-accelerated systems, continuously expanding the frontier of scientific discovery. With the emergence of quantum processing units (QPUs) as practical computational accelerators, a new opportunity arises to further extend this trajectory by integrating quantum and classical computing paradigms.

items.title: Multidimensional revival dynamics in a bosonic many-body system
items.summary: The collapse and revival of localized states in many-body systems is a quintessential example of a quantum interference phenomenon that cannot be explained purely within mean-field theories. Historically, the majority of previous work on quantum revivals has been in a Schrödinger mechanics context, typically for effectively 1D systems with a focus on the autocorrelation function as the key detection observable.

items.title: QSoftCore: A Conceptual Foundation for Quantum Software Engineering
items.summary: Quantum software engineering (QSE) requires understanding application requirements, quantum programs and algorithms, quantum computation paradigms, executions, and deployment. However, relevant quantum computing (QC) concepts are often defined across physical, mathematical, and paradigm-specific levels of abstraction, making it difficult for the QSE community and hence proposed methods to refer to them consistently.

items.title: Colloquium: Quantum information processing with ensembles of identical particles
items.summary: Identical particles underpin most quantum technologies, but the role of indistinguishability in these processes extends far beyond the symmetrization of many-particle states. This Colloquium presents a unified operational perspective on how particle identity, indistinguishability, exchange statistics, and many-particle interference can instead be harnessed as resources for quantum information processing.
